assumptions: USA: Declaration of Use (§8) deadline = US Registration Date + 6 years (window opens at 5th anniversary); 6-month grace with fees.
USA: Declaration of Use / Renewal (§8 & §9) = US Registration Date + 10 years (window opens at 9th anniversary), then every 10 years.
USA: US dates run from the US registration date, not the Madrid Protocol date.
Madrid: IR renewal = IR registration date + 10 years.
Madrid: WIPO irregularities notice response = notice date + 3 months (assumed standard WIPO period).

Philippines: DAU also due 3 years from filing — applies to national applications, Madrid Protocol designations and subsequent designations alike. For Madrid cases the 3 years is assumed to run from the IR date (or the subsequent designation date); log that date as Application Filed on the designation case.
Philippines: DAU after renewal = renewal date + 1 year.
Mexico: DAU = WIPO renewal notice received + 3 months (manual trigger — log the notice date on the case).
Philippines and Mexico dates should be entered on both the IR case and the country designation case.

templates.subject: Our Ref: [FileNumber] - [MatterName] - [TrademarkName] in [RegistrationClasses] in [Jurisdiction]
templates.body:
Dear [FirstName]

We confirm that the application to register the mark [TrademarkName] in [RegistrationClasses] was filed with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (PTO).

Details of your trade mark application as filed are below.

Applicant: [CompanyName]
Trade Mark: [TrademarkName]
Serial Number: [ApplicationNumber]
Goods & Services: [GoodsServices]
Filing Date: [ApplicationFiled]

We expect it will be around 9-10 months before we hear from an examining attorney at the PTO regarding this application. Upon examining the application, the examiner will issue either an Office Action raising questions or objections concerning the application or a Notice of Publication indicating that the application has been preliminarily approved for publication in the Trademark Official Gazette. The US application was filed based on the Australian application, so will require the Australian application to become registered before it can be registered itself. We will advise you when we receive anything further from the PTO relating to this application.

Until such time as this application is granted registration by the PTO, the Company should use the ™ symbol in conjunction with the first prominent use of the [TrademarkName] mark on any Web page, products, packaging, promotional literature, and elsewhere. If you have any questions about such usage, please let us know. We encourage the Company to begin using the ™ symbol immediately, but please note that it is not appropriate or permissible to use the ® symbol in conjunction with the trademark until the mark is granted a U.S. registration for these goods/services.

Finally, please note that United States trademark application and registration records are public information. A number of private companies harvest such information from the PTO database and send trademark owners solicitations or fake "invoices" for the purchase of various goods and services. Such correspondence often is designed to look as if it came from the Patent and Trademark Office itself or from some other official-sounding agency. If the Company receives a solicitation or request for money from any entity other than brandU Legal, please do not hesitate to forward such communications to us for confirmation that they can be ignored.

We will continue to monitor your application and will contact you with any further developments. In the meantime if you have questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.

templates.subject: Our Ref: [FileNumber] - [CompanyName] - [TrademarkName], [RegistrationNumber] in [RegistrationClasses] in [Jurisdiction]
templates.body:
Dear [FirstName],

We have received the certificate of registration for [TrademarkName] in the US and attach the certificate for your files. The trade mark has been assigned Registration No. [RegistrationNumber]. Please note that the United States Patent and Trade Mark Office (USPTO) does not issue hard copies of the certificate.

In order to keep this registration in effect, it will be necessary to file a Declaration of Use between the fifth and sixth year after the date of registration (this initial deadline is [US-DeadlineforDecofUse5thAnniversary]). The client must subsequently file a Declaration of Use/Renewal Application between the ninth and tenth year after the date of registration (this subsequent deadline is [US-DeadlineforDecofUse10thAnniversary]), and each successive ten-year period thereafter.

Trademark rights are not retained merely by owning a registration. A trademark must be used with sufficient frequency and in such a manner as to evidence an intention to use it. Interrupted, sporadic or isolated usage can result in the loss of ownership of a trademark. In addition, if you become aware of any other person using a confusingly similar trademark, it is important to take prompt action to preserve your rights.

Please be aware that a number of private companies not associated with the USPTO often use trademark application and registration information from the USPTO's database to mail or email trademark-related solicitations. To further confuse recipients, a number of these companies have adopted very official sounding names, so that recipients will think that the company is a government entity. As a general rule, if you receive an unsolicited communication that requests payment for trademark-related services, it is likely that the communication is a scam.

When using your trade mark, you should use the mark precisely in the form in which it is registered. If you use a mark which is more than slightly different from your registered mark, the use of the altered mark may not count as use to maintain the validity of the registered mark.

Now that this mark is registered, some form of registration notice should be included in all advertising and other printed usages of the mark in connection with the goods and/or services listed in the registration (although this is not a mandatory requirement for the US). The ® symbol, or other references to the mark being registered, including "Reg. U.S. Pat. And TM Off." or "Registered in U.S. Patent and Trademark Office" should only be used if your mark is registered.

If there is a name and/or address change or the mark is assigned or licenced to another party, the change/licence should be recorded with the USPTO.

Finally, you may wish to consider recording this registration with the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). CBP can deny importation of articles into the US bearing a mark or name "copying or simulating" a recorded mark. Goods bearing such marks can be detained, seized, and forfeited by CBP. The primary benefit of recording a trade mark with CBP is that any goods bearing counterfeit marks or "copying or simulating" marks may be detained prior to entry into the US at minimal cost to the owner of the mark. Please let us know if you would like further information about recording this mark with CBP.

We trust that the above information is clear. If however you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.

We would like to take this opportunity to thank you for your instructions in this matter.

templates.subject: Re: US Registration for [TrademarkName] in the name of [CompanyName] - Reminder for Declaration of Use and Incontestibility - Registration No. [RegistrationNumber]
templates.body:
Dear [FirstName]

In order to maintain the above US registration for its full ten year term, a declaration of use must be filed for the registration between now and [US-DeadlineforDecofUse5thAnniversary]. The declarations of use may be filed up to six months later upon the payment of additional government fees.

It may also be possible to combine each declaration of use with a declaration of "incontestability," if (1) the mark has been in continuous use for the five years since the issuance of the registration, (2) the registration is not the subject of any action pending in the courts or before the USPTO, and (3) there has been no decision adverse to the registrant's right to register the mark or keep it on the Register.

Can you please let us know if you wish to maintain the registration for [TrademarkName] in the US and we will provide you with details of next steps and costs.

We look forward to hearing from you. If you have any questions, please let us know.

templates.dateField: US Declaration of Use / Renewal (9th-10th year)
templates.subject: Re: [CompanyName] - Notice of Acceptance of Section 8 and 15 Declaration of Use and Incontestibility for [TrademarkName], Registration No. [RegistrationNumber]
templates.body:
Hi [FirstName],

I am pleased to inform you that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has accepted the declaration of use and incontestability for the above referenced registration.

The registration will remain in force for the remainder of the ten-year term, i.e., until [RenewalDeadline]. At that time, the registration may be renewed for an additional ten-year term, provided the mark is in use in the United States. In addition, your right to use the mark is now "incontestable" and can only be challenged on very limited grounds, such as abandonment, that the mark has become generic, and fraud.

Declaration of Use
You must file a declaration of use (or excusable non-use) and an application for renewal between the 9th and 10th year after the registration date, that is by [US-DeadlineforDecofUse10thAnniversary].

We have entered the renewal deadline into our trade mark database and will contact you closer to the time concerning the renewal requirements. Although we will endeavour to contact you, we accept no responsibility for doing so, and therefore recommend that you maintain your own record for these deadlines.

If you have any questions regarding this mark or registration, please don't hesitate to contact us.

templates.stage: IR renewal reminder (incl. Mexico / Philippines / US DAU notes)
templates.subject: [FileNumber] [CompanyName] - [RegistrationNumber] - [TrademarkName] in [Jurisdiction]
templates.body:
Dear [FirstName]

We wish to inform you that [RegistrationNumber] for [TrademarkName] is due for renewal on [RenewalDeadline].

As this is an international registration (IR) filed via the Madrid Protocol, one renewal application is filed via the World Intellectual Property Office (WIPO), there is no requirement to renew the trade mark in each designated country.

The renewal fees are:
- Our professional fees to arrange this and to maintain the registration for a further 10 years - $[FEES] + GST
- Govt Fees - $[GOVT FEES]
- Total - $[TOTAL] + GST

PLEASE INCLUDE THE BELOW IF MEXICO IS A DESIGNATION
Be aware however that some countries have maintenance requirements including:
1. Mexico - in order to maintain the trade mark in Mexico, a Declaration of Actual Use (DAU) must be filed directly with the Mexican Trade Marks Office within three (3) months of receiving the notice of renewal of the IR from WIPO. We will advise you of this date once we receive notification thereof from WIPO.
2. Philippines - in order to maintain the trade mark in the Philippines, a DAU must be filed directly with the Philippines Trade Marks Office within one (1) year from the date of renewal of registration, namely by [Philippines-Renewal-1stanniversarydeadline].
3. US - in order to maintain the trade mark in the US, a DAU must be filed directly with the USPTO between the 9th and 10th years after the US registration date. We will email you separately in this regard.

In light of the above, please confirm whether you wish to renew the [RegistrationNumber] for [TrademarkName] at your earliest convenience to avoid inadvertent expiry of the mark.

The deadline to file the DAU for Mexico is [Mexico-WIPORenewalNoticeDate].
Please confirm as soon as possible whether you have used the trade mark in Mexico so we can arrange for our associates to prepare the DAU.

PLEASE INCLUDE THE BELOW IF PHILIPPINES IS A DESIGNATION
As the Philippines is designated under this international registration and as previously advised, if you wish to maintain the trade mark in the Philippines, a DAU must be filed directly with the Philippines Trade Marks Office within one (1) year from the date of renewal of registration, namely by [Philippines-Renewal-1stanniversarydeadline].
Please confirm as soon as possible whether you have used the trade mark in the Philippines so we can arrange for our associates to prepare the DAU.

We will email you separately in this regard.
